This game.. Oh man this game. This game is the greatest story, decision making game I have played this year! Let me go over many of the gameplay and story and rate them accordingly.

GAMEPLAY: Gameplay in this game is very, very simple. You just click a statement and drag it too the character it corresponds with. Sometimes you'll get a yellow highlight on text, or AKA a conflicting statement to another statement. This means you have two or more choices too pick from. All choices usually have something different and the game and the advisor will react differently depending on the choice you make. I'll make one up for you if this makes no sense too you; There's one statement "I love this band!" and then there's another statement/post "That lady (talking about the person who said the first statement) hates that band!" Now, you have to decide which is true, or if you want, decide which is false ;) but usually them hating the band or not does not matter as that's not important to the STORY, which I'll get to in a moment. There's also going through text messages, listening to conversations and even going through phones and desktops. For this game, you are a investigator, so you will have to think a bit too determine what you want Orwell to know.  It might sound boring to others, but it's actually not. It can get intense and fun if you put your mind to it. Now, the MAIN thing this game has going for it is it's great STORY!

STORY: A short summary of the game story goes like this: You are a investigator, trying to solve who did a series of consecutive bombings around "The Nation".  That's basically it without spoiling it. The game's story goes indepth, into telling you directly and indirectly. There's websites in the game that have a lot of information about what is happening out in the world. Because of this, I felt so immersed, like there was actual events going on out in the world that you don't see at all. The main story can get a bit twisty too and is great for people who like criminal investigations. I, personally found myself being in love with some of the characters. This was an awesome experience and can't wait to get the sequel!

OVERALL SCORE: 10/10 BOIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIIS.

Some pros and cons i would like to point out -

Pros 
- Solid game with a proper story and atmosphere to match it.
- Choices there is no game over you play the game and finish in the way you want.
- Covers a lot of real world apps that you can easily connect the dots too.
- Sweet twists in plot will have you clicking around furiously....hehe

Cons
- There is a insanely long load time once you start the game causing many people to think maybe the game is stuck. Also pain if you happened to close the game by mistake will have to sit through the loading again.
- sometimes the hitbox completely misses what you select , this could be a disaster if there is a timed event going on, also for some reason overlay might stop responding (chapter 5)
- Sometimes the indicator which shows whats new to check out might not update casuing you to think that you missed reading something, also sometimes that hints are pretty vaugue leading to some annoying going back to older articles to check if something was missed.
- The ending ....it barely points to anything that there will be a second part or some shocking end game story<after credits> hinting to a second game but if you check the steam store there is a follow up game to this :D .

Overall if you are in the dark as to way some people are extermely worried/against letting their privacy lost that easily check this game out , loved it easily a 8/10.

I had my eye on 'Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You' for some time already, and was lucky enough to pick it up for free on Humble a while ago.

Besides presenting the gameplay in a very clear way through the Orwell module, it's a game with a message as well: I found its take on the ever-popular social debate of privacy vs security very interesting, without getting too preachy either way. It does make you think!

The first playthrough took me roughly five hours, the second playthrough took me a bit over three hours. Replayability beyond that is limited, as one would expect from an investigation game... while there are different outcomes for most characters you investigate depending on the information you pass on or omit as an investigator, the story in general is fairly linear. Once the rabbit is out of the hat and the mystery is gone, the only remaining fun is to figure out what happens if you do things differently (often: sub-optimally, depending on how seriously you take your role as investigator and how much you're willing to let characters off the hook for stuff you find out about them).

All in all I must say I've had a very good time with this game. I personally wouldn't buy it for full price (even after having played it and knowing how much I enjoyed it) given the limited amount of hours I got out of it, but I would definitely recommend picking it up when it's on sale.
